questions.problem:
For the universal set $U,$ given by

$$
U={2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9},
$$

find the truth set of $P(x)⇒Q(x)$ for the following predicates: 

- $P(x):$ $x$ is prime.

- $Q(x):$ $3\,|\,x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $P(x)⇒Q(x)≡¬P(x)∨Q(x),$ the corresponding truth sets can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇒Q} & ={T}_{¬P∨Q} \\  & ={T}_{¬P}\cup {T}_{Q} \\  & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note the following:

- The truth set of $P(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{P}={2,3,5,7}.
$$

As a result, the complement is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{T}}_{P} & =\overset{―}{{2,3,5,7}} \\  & ={4,6,8,9}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The truth set of $Q(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{Q}={3,6,9}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇒Q} & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q} \\  & ={4,6,8,9}\cup {3,6,9} \\  & ={3,4,6,8,9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the truth set of $P(x)⇒Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $R:$ 

- $P(x):$ $4x-7\ge 9$

- $Q(x):$ $0<x<5$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $P(x)⇒Q(x)≡¬P(x)∨Q(x),$ the corresponding truth sets can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇒Q} & ={T}_{¬P∨Q} \\  & ={T}_{¬P}\cup {T}_{Q} \\  & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note the following:

- To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-7 & \ge 9 \\ 4x & \ge 16 \\ x & \ge 4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is
${T}_{P}=[4,\infty ).$
As a result, the complement is
${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}=(-\infty ,4).$

- The truth set of $Q(x)$ is 
${T}_{Q}=(0,5).$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇒Q} & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q} \\  & =(-\infty ,4)\cup (0,5) \\  & =(-\infty ,5).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $R:$

- $P(x):$ $4x-7\ge 9$

- $Q(x):$ $0<x<5$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we have that

$$
P(x)⇔Q(x)≡(P(x)∧Q(x))∨(¬P(x)∧¬Q(x)),
$$

 

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇔Q}=({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note the following:

- To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-7 & \ge 9 \\ 4x & \ge 16 \\ x & \ge 4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is
${T}_{P}=[4,\infty ).$
As a result, the complement is
${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}=(-\infty ,4).$

- The truth set of $Q(x)$ is 
${T}_{Q}=(0,5)$ 
and its complement is
${\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}=(-\infty ,0]\cup [5,\infty ).$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q} & =[4,\infty )\cap (0,5) \\  & =[4,5) \\ {\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q} & =(-\infty ,4)\cap ((-\infty ,0]\cup [5,\infty )) \\  & =(-\infty ,0] \\ {T}_{P⇔Q} & =({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}) \\  & =[4,5)\cup (-\infty ,0] \\  & =(-\infty ,0]\cup [4,5).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
For the universal set $U,$ given by

$$
U={2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10},
$$

find the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x)$ for the following predicates: 

- $P(x):$ $x$ is composite

- $Q(x):$ $10$ is divisible by $x$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we have that

$$
P(x)⇔Q(x)≡(P(x)∧Q(x))∨(¬P(x)∧¬Q(x)),
$$

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇔Q}=({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q})\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that:

- The truth set of $P(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{P}={4,6,8,9,10}
$$

and its complement is

$$
{\overset{―}{T}}_{P}={2,3,5,7}.
$$

- The truth set of $Q(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{Q}={2,5,10}
$$

 
and its complement is

$$
{\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}={3,4,6,7,8,9}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q} & ={4,6,8,9,10}\cap {2,5,10} \\  & ={10} \\ {\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q} & ={2,3,5,7}\cap {3,4,6,7,8,9} \\  & ={3,7} \\ {T}_{P⇔Q} & =({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}) \\  & ={10}\cup {3,7} \\  & ={3,7,10}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$\,$ If $x$ has more than three divisors, then $x$ is composite.

Which of the following is logically equivalent to the conditional predicate above?
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote by $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ the following predicates:

- $P(x):$ $x$ has more than three divisors.

- $Q(x):$ $x$ is composite.

Then, our initial sentence can be written as $P(x)⇒Q(x),$ which is logically equivalent to 

$$
¬P(x)∨Q(x).
$$

The negation of $P(x)$ can be written as

- $¬P(x):$ $x$ doesn't have more than three divisors.

Therefore, the given sentence is logically equivalent to the following:

$\,$ $x$ doesn't have more than three divisors, or $x$ is composite.

$x$ doesn't have more than three divisors, and $x$ is composite.

questions.problem:
Consider the following predicates.

$\,$ $A(x):$ $3\,|\,x.$ $\,$ $B(x):$ $3\,|\,(x+15).$

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate $A(x)⇔B(x)?$

- $3\,|\,x$ if and only if $5\,|x.$
- If $3\,|\,x$ then $3\,|\,(x+15),$ or if $3\,|\,(x+15)$ then $3\,|\,x.$
- If $3\,|\,x$ then $3\,|\,(x+15),$ and if $3\,|\,(x+15)$ then $3\,|\,x.$
questions.worked_solution:
A biconditional expression $P⇔Q≡(P⇒Q)∧(Q⇒P)$ can be read as shown below:

- $P$ if and only if $Q$

- $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

- If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

So, $A⇔B$ translates into the following sentences:

- $3\,|\,x$ if and only if $3\,|\,(x+15).$

- $3\,|\,x$ is equivalent to $3\,|\,(x+15).$

- If $3\,|\,x$ then $3\,|\,(x+15),$ and if $3\,|\,(x+15)$ then $3\,|\,x.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

mathematical_assessment.explanation: Rechecking: 3 divides x exactly when it divides x+15, so A⇔B is always true. II and III are therefore both equivalent to it for these predicates. I is false at x=3. The mathematically correct combination, “II and III only,” is missing. “III only” fits the general biconditional expansion but excludes II despite the specific arithmetic equivalence; this caused the earlier uncertainty.

questions.problem:
Consider the following predicates.

$\,$ $A(x):$ $x\in {-1,0,3,7}\cap N.$ $\,$ $B(x):$ $x\in {3,7}.$ 

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate $A(x)⇔B(x)?$

- $x\in {-1,0,3,7}\cap N$ is equivalent to  $x\in N.$
- $x\in {-1,0,3,7}\cap N$ if and only if $x\in {3,7}.$
- If $x\in {-1,0,3,7}\cap N$ then $x\in {3,7},$ or if $x\in {3,7}$ then $x\in {-1,0,3,7}\cap N.$
questions.worked_solution:
A biconditional expression $P⇔Q≡(P⇒Q)∧(Q⇒P)$ can be read as shown below:

- $P$ if and only if $Q$

- $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

- If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

So, $A⇔B$ translates into the following sentences:

- $x\in {-1,0,3,7}\cap N$ if and only if $x\in {3,7}.$

- $x\in {-1,0,3,7}\cap N$ is equivalent to $x\in {3,7}.$

- If $x\in {-1,0,3,7}\cap N$ then $x\in {3,7},$ and if $x\in {3,7}$ then $x\in {-1,0,3,7}\cap N.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

mathematical_assessment.explanation: II exactly restates the biconditional. I fails at x=1. III is always true because B implies A. If N includes 0, A⇔B is false at x=0, so only II is equivalent (d). If N excludes 0, A=B, so II and III are equivalent (e). The unspecified convention for N causes the earlier uncertainty; d also matches the lesson's structural reading.

Since we have that

$$
P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x) \equiv \big(P(x) \land Q(x)\big) \lor \big(\neg P(x) \land \neg Q(x)\big),
$$

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇔Q}=({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q})\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that:

- The truth set of $P(x)$ is 

$$
T_P = \big\{ 2,4,6,8,10 \big\}
$$

and its complement is

$$
\overline{T}_P 
%= \overline{\big\{ 4,6,8,9,10 \big\}} 
= \big\{1,3,5,7,9 \big\}.
$$

- The truth set of $Q(x)$ is 

$$
T_Q = \big\{ 1,2,3,4,6 \big\}
$$

 
and its complement is

$$
\overline{T}_Q 
%= \overline{\big\{ \big\}} 
= \big\{ 5,7,8,9,10  \big\}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q} & ={2,4,6,8,10}\cap {1,2,3,4,6} \\  & ={2,4,6} \\ {\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q} & ={1,3,5,7,9}\cap {5,7,8,9,10} \\  & ={5,7,9} \\ {T}_{P⇔Q} & =({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}) \\  & ={2,4,6}\cup {5,7,9} \\  & ={2,4,5,6,7,9}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the following predicates.

$\qquad$ $A(x):$ $x<4.$ $\qquad$ $B(x):$ $\dfrac x2< 2.$

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate $A(x) \Leftrightarrow B(x)?$

- $x<4$ if and only if $\dfrac x2< 2.$

- $x<4$ is equivalent to $\dfrac x2< 2.$

- If $x<4$ then $\dfrac x2< 2,$ or if $\dfrac x2< 2$ then $x <4.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
A biconditional expression $P \Leftrightarrow Q \equiv (P \Rightarrow Q) \land (Q \Rightarrow P)$ can be read as shown below:

- $P$ if and only if $Q$

- $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

- If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

So, $A \Leftrightarrow B$ translates into the following sentences:

- $x<4$ if and only if $\dfrac x2< 2.$

- $x<4$ is equivalent to $\dfrac x2< 2.$

- If $x<4$ then $\dfrac x2< 2,$ and if $\dfrac x2< 2$ then $x <4.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
